design.md's Constraint Compliance section (lines 988-999) covers 8 named constraints comprehensively (no new loop-inventory entry, no new suite file, assert_terminal/assert_artifacts_schema unmodified, emit-run-record.sh byte-identical, REQ-007 degradation, PROJECT_CONTEXT_INVALID distinguishability, golden-baseline write protection, cross-epic citation drift) with no gaps found there. However, design.md's own Compatibility Matrix (F4 row, REQ-002 column) states AC-007's disposition as 'SKIP-with-activation → AC-007 (until Epic A1 **and** Epic A4 both merge)' -- this directly contradicts requirements.md's own AC-007 text, which states the activation condition is 'Epic A4 merged to main' (a single dependency, no Epic A1 clause: '...until Epic A4's Facet Manifest exists, activation condition "Epic A4 merged to main" (REQ-007)'), and it also contradicts design.md's own worked REQ-007 skip-allowlist-manifest/v1 JSON example (Data Plan), whose AC-007 entry lists only a single {epic: A4, issue: 192} dependency with activation_condition: 'merged(A4)' -- no merged(A1) clause. A Phase 2/3 implementer following the Compatibility Matrix table versus the manifest JSON example (or requirements.md's own AC-007 definition) would build two non-interoperable activation conditions for the identical assertion, exactly the kind of silent drift REQ-007's own fingerprint-drift mechanism (AC-035c) is designed to catch elsewhere in this same package. This is not owned by precheck (design_req_drift: false only checks hash/status drift, not AC-level cross-section contradiction) and is not duplicated by any other check in this report.

High-risk surfaces (B1 golden-baseline write-authority, B2 shared-registry blast radius, B3 REQ-007 allowlist fail-open closure, B4 cross-epic fingerprint-citation drift, B5 structural-comparison tamper-resistance) each have a concrete, correctly-cited validation path (AC-040/AC-041, AC-008/AC-009/AC-011, AC-035, AC-035c, AC-030/AC-031 respectively). However, the Compatibility Matrix's own Disposition legend requires every SKIP-with-activation cell to cite '<AC-id> (a named SKIP degrading per that AC's own REQ-007 allowlist-manifest entry... until its activation_condition evaluates true)' -- i.e., the assertion's own AC, not the manifest-shape-defining AC-034. Design.md's F3 row (REQ-002 column) and F3/F4 rows (REQ-003 column) instead cite 'SKIP-with-activation → AC-034's F3/F4 entry', violating this self-stated rule: AC-034 defines the skip-allowlist-manifest/v1 schema's own shape (requirements.md: 'lists every upstream-dependent assertion... each row's own dependencies field...'), not a substantive assertion with its own activation_condition. For the REQ-003 cells the correct citation exists and should have been used (AC-010/AC-025, the quality-gate-outcome capability_applicability assertion driven by TEST-019, requirements.md AC-010/AC-025) but is not cited. For F3's REQ-002 (structural, Context-present-advisory) cell, no acceptance criterion anywhere in requirements.md or acceptance-tests.md defines what the advisory-state structural assertion actually checks -- AC-005 covers only Context-absent generation (F1/F2), AC-007 covers only Context-present-required (F4/F6) Facet-reference-absence -- yet the Observable×fixture-state judgment table (design.md, immediately below the Compatibility Matrix) marks F3's 'Generated-artifact structure' observable as 'structural', asserting a comparison exists. F3's REQ-002 structural risk surface therefore has no concretely named verification path at all, and the F3/F4 REQ-003 risk surface's stated path points to the wrong acceptance criterion.
